showFullCode.title: Show Complete File
showFullCode.description: Show complete file for code, with bootstrap and error handling included.

AiBriefHttpRequest.title: AiBriefHttpRequest
AiBriefHttpRequest.description: What the console may send: the stage and, for disputes, which case. Session facts are never caller input.

AupCategorySignalResponse.title: AupCategorySignalResponse
AupCategorySignalResponse.description: Optional Channel3 signal shown next to the AUP result; it never changes the rule decision.

CaseRouteResponse.title: CaseRouteResponse
CaseRouteResponse.description: Fuzzy case routing: which goods group (and so which dispute items) applies. Code decides; advisory only.

ConnectionsResponse.title: ConnectionsResponse
ConnectionsResponse.description: Deployment mode only. Never a key, a key's presence, a value or a variable name.

CountryRulesCheckRequest.title: CountryRulesCheckRequest
CountryRulesCheckRequest.description: Seller and buyer countries plus closed choices; no free text reaches the check.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: The error body every refusal uses.

GuideFormRequest.title: GuideFormRequest
GuideFormRequest.description: One field ({item, value}) or one round of up to three fields ({fields: [...]}), never both.

ProductCard.title: ProductCard
ProductCard.description: A Channel3 catalogue product reduced to what identifies the item; no prices, offers or buy links.

ProductConfirmResponse.title: ProductConfirmResponse
ProductConfirmResponse.description: The seller's own choice: one of the cards they were shown, or none of them.

ProductReferenceResponse.title: ProductReferenceResponse
ProductReferenceResponse.description: Up to three Channel3 products for the seller to pick from; advisory, never changes the AUP decision.

SendGuard.title: SendGuard
SendGuard.description: (r25 send guard) What a send carries and to whom, side by side; every account id is masked (first 2, last 4).

SentFileFingerprint.title: SentFileFingerprint
SentFileFingerprint.description:
Plain SHA-256 of one file's exact bytes, recorded at the moment of a send so a later read-back can be compared.

The keyed ``payload_sha256`` cannot be checked outside the session; this one can. Never present on a preview.

SyntheticMoney.title: SyntheticMoney
SyntheticMoney.description: Same shape as the PayPal Disputes `dispute_amount` (ProviderMoney below); values are synthetic.

WebhookEventProjection.title: WebhookEventProjection
WebhookEventProjection.description: All that is kept after a SUCCESS: identifiers and status only, no amounts, payer data, links or summary.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason, for example session_required.

message.description: A plain sentence for a person.

X-CSRF-Token.description: CSRF token for the same session. Get it from the csrf_token field of the response to POST /api/v1/demo/sessions. Every POST also needs it; without it the API answers 403 csrf_rejected.

X-Demo-Session.description: Demo session id. Get it from the session_id field of the response to POST /api/v1/demo/sessions (that request needs no header). Without it the API answers 401 session_required.

Title: Getting Started with TradeGlot Local Console

Nodes.Text: API of the local TradeGlot console (127.0.0.1:8000). It uses synthetic data, expects the demo session headers the console sets, and the hosted demo answers 503 on every route that would reach PayPal. Authentication: create a session with POST /api/v1/demo/sessions, then send X-Demo-Session on every other call and X-CSRF-Token on every POST. POST calls also need an Origin header equal to the console's own origin (browsers add it; scripts must set it), otherwise the API answers 403 origin_required.

You must have Python ```3.7+``` installed on your system to install and run this SDK. This SDK package depends on other Python packages like pytest, etc. These dependencies are defined in the ```requirements.txt``` file that comes with the SDK. To resolve these dependencies, you can use the PIP Dependency manager. Install it by following steps at [https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installing/](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installing/).

Python and PIP executables should be defined in your PATH. Open command prompt and type ```pip --version```. This should display the version of the PIP Dependency Manager installed if your installation was successful and the paths are properly defined.

* Using command line, navigate to the directory containing the generated files (including ```requirements.txt```) for the SDK.
* Run the command ```pip install -r requirements.txt```. This should install all the required dependencies.

Nodes.Text: The API client can be initialized as follows:
Code-Based Client Initialization

from tradeglotlocalconsole.configuration import Environment
from tradeglotlocalconsole.http.auth.demo_csrf import DemoCsrfCredentials
from tradeglotlocalconsole.http.auth.demo_session import DemoSessionCredentials
from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient(
    demo_csrf_credentials=DemoCsrfCredentials(
        x_csrf_token='X-CSRF-Token'
    ),
    demo_session_credentials=DemoSessionCredentials(
        x_demo_session='X-Demo-Session'
    ),
    environment=Environment.PRODUCTION
)
Environment-Based Client Initialization

from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

# Specify the path to your .env file if it’s located outside the project’s root directory.
client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient.from_environment(dotenv_path='/path/to/.env')
See the [Environment-Based Client Initialization]($h/__additional_documentation/Configuration/Environment-Based%20Client%20Initialization) section for details.

This API uses the following authentication schemes.
* [`DemoCsrf (Custom Header Signature)`]($h/__auth_DemoCsrf)
* [`DemoSession (Custom Header Signature)`]($h/__auth_DemoSession)
Documentation for accessing and setting credentials for DemoCsrf.

Data: CSRF token for the same session. Get it from the csrf_token field of the response to POST /api/v1/demo/sessions. Every POST also needs it; without it the API answers 403 csrf_rejected.

Nodes.Text: **Note:** Auth credentials can be set using `DemoCsrfCredentials` object, passed in as named parameter `demo_csrf_credentials` in the client initialization.
You must provide credentials in the client as shown in the following code snippet.

from tradeglotlocalconsole.http.auth.demo_csrf import DemoCsrfCredentials
from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient(
    demo_csrf_credentials=DemoCsrfCredentials(
        x_csrf_token='X-CSRF-Token'
    )
)
Documentation for accessing and setting credentials for DemoSession.

Data: Demo session id. Get it from the session_id field of the response to POST /api/v1/demo/sessions (that request needs no header). Without it the API answers 401 session_required.

Nodes.Text: **Note:** Auth credentials can be set using `DemoSessionCredentials` object, passed in as named parameter `demo_session_credentials` in the client initialization.
You must provide credentials in the client as shown in the following code snippet.

from tradeglotlocalconsole.http.auth.demo_session import DemoSessionCredentials
from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient(
    demo_session_credentials=DemoSessionCredentials(
        x_demo_session='X-Demo-Session'
    )
)

Nodes.Title: Use the rule checks from an AI agent (MCP)

Nodes.Text: The repository ships a small read-only MCP server, `src/payguard/mcp_server.py`, built on the Python standard library. It speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio.

| Tool | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `check_acceptable_use` | A review signal for a product description. |
| `list_countries` | The ten countries in the rules pack. |
| `check_country_rules` | Findings for a seller and buyer country, most severe first, each with its source. |
| `search_rule_clauses` | The best matches among 140 paraphrased PayPal clauses. |
| `check_sales_spike` | A comparison with a baseline you declare; the answer says the baseline is unverified. |
There is no tool that sends evidence, connects to PayPal, approves or changes anything.
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -B -m payguard.mcp_server

Nodes.Title: What TradeGlot is, and what it is not

Nodes.Text: TradeGlot gives small PayPal sellers rule checks and a gated evidence workflow. Everything in this API documentation describes the **local console** (127.0.0.1:8000) and runs on **synthetic data** against the **PayPal Sandbox**.

- Advisory only: every answer is a review signal. It is not a compliance decision and not legal advice.
- A person approves every send: one tick, then two presses. The hosted demo makes no PayPal calls and answers `503 hosted_demo_disabled` on every route that would.
- The AI step (Gemini) only picks from closed options and its picks are checked by rules. It does not guess and does not decide who wins.
- PayPal and the card issuer make every real decision.

from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

Nodes.Text: The SDK client can also be initialized directly from environment variables using the `from_environment()` class method. This allows the SDK to automatically read configuration values from the runtime environment or a .env file.
Example

from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

# Specify the path to your .env file if it’s located outside the project’s root directory.
client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient.from_environment(dotenv_path='/path/to/.env')
You can also specify a path to a `.env` file by passing it to the `from_environment()` method:

The same method can accept keyword arguments to override any values read from the environment, and the arguments to override values should follow the same approach as code-based client initialization.

from tradeglotlocalconsole.tradeglotlocalconsole_client import TradeglotlocalconsoleClient

client = TradeglotlocalconsoleClient.from_environment(
    dotenv_path='/path/to/.env',
    timeout=0,  # overrides timeout from environment variable
)
Values provided through arguments take precedence over those defined in environment variables.
Example `.env` File

ENVIRONMENT=production

DEMO_CSRF_X_CSRF_TOKEN=ExampleXCSRFToken
DEMO_SESSION_X_DEMO_SESSION=ExampleXDemoSession

TIMEOUT=60
MAX_RETRIES=3
BACKOFF_FACTOR=2
RETRY_STATUSES=408,413
RETRY_METHODS=GET,PUT,DELETE

# Proxy Configuration
PROXY_ADDRESS=https://jiarong0423.github.io/payguard-ai/portal
PROXY_PORT=8080
PROXY_USERNAME=username
PROXY_PASSWORD=password
Note
- If an environment variable is not defined, the default SDK configuration value will be used.
